definitions.explanation: Relating to or conforming to principles of right and wrong conduct. Describes behavior, judgments, or standards that align with accepted moral principles.

examples.japanese: {道徳的|どうとくてき}な{判断|はんだん}が{求|もと}められる。
それは{道徳的|どうとくてき}に{問題|もんだい}がある{行為|こうい}だ。
examples.english: That is an act that is morally problematic.

examples.japanese: {法律|ほうりつ}に{違反|いはん}しなくても、{道徳的|どうとくてき}に{許|ゆる}されないこともある。
examples.english: Even if something doesn't violate the law, it may be morally unacceptable.

notes:
USAGE:
The na-adjective form of {道徳|どうとく} (morality, ethics) + {的|てき} (suffix forming adjectives). Used to describe actions, people, or standards in terms of right and wrong. Can modify nouns ({道徳的|どうとくてき}な + noun) or be used adverbially ({道徳的|どうとくてき}に).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {道徳的|どうとくてき}な{判断|はんだん} (moral judgment)
- {道徳的|どうとくてき}な{責任|せきにん} (moral responsibility)
- {道徳的|どうとくてき}に{正|ただ}しい (morally right)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {倫理的|りんりてき}: ethical — very similar but more academic/philosophical
- {不道徳|ふどうとく}: immoral — the negative form
